title: Psalm 130: Out of the Depths
summary: From the depths the psalmist cries to the LORD and asks to be heard. If God kept a record of sins no one could stand, but with him there is forgiveness, and so the psalmist waits for the LORD more than night watchmen wait for morning. He ends by calling all Israel to hope in the LORD, who has steadfast love, abundant redemption, and will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.

line: From the depths the psalmist cries to the LORD; if God kept a record of sins no one could stand, but with him there is forgiveness, so he waits more than watchmen wait for morning.
guide: If you fear your wrongs are too many, verses 3 and 4 say God does not keep score that way. Pray verse 1 from wherever you are. The psalm does not promise when the morning comes, only that it will; when you find hope in the depths, pass it on.

care.text: If ‘the depths’ describe your life now, and the night feels long, please do not carry it alone. The man who prayed this psalm was still waiting when it ended. Waiting is not a failure of faith. Tell someone you trust: a doctor, a pastor or a friend. If you have thoughts of hurting yourself, speak to someone today. The Find Help page on this site lists places to turn.

stanzas.title: If you kept a record, who could stand? But with you is forgiveness
Waiting like watchmen for the morning
Israel, hope in the LORD, who will redeem

verses.t: A song of ascents. Out of the depths I cry to You, O LORD!
O Lord, hear my voice; let Your ears be attentive to my plea for mercy.
If You, O LORD, kept track of iniquities, then who, O Lord, could stand?
But with You there is forgiveness, so that You may be feared.
I wait for the LORD; my soul does wait, and in His word I put my hope.
My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning— more than watchmen wait for the morning.
O Israel, put your hope in the LORD, for with the LORD is loving devotion, and with Him is redemption in abundance.
And He will redeem Israel from all iniquity.
